interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between JVM, JRE, and JDK?
interviewQuestions.answer: JDK (Java Development Kit) contains tools needed to develop Java programs including javac compiler. JRE (Java Runtime Environment) provides libraries and JVM to execute programs. JVM (Java Virtual Machine) executes compiled bytecode, managing memory allocation, garbage collection, and platform independence.

interviewQuestions.question: Why is the String class immutable in Java?
interviewQuestions.answer: String immutability provides security (safe for database URLs and passwords), thread safety (multiple threads can read without synchronization), caching efficiency (allows the String Constant Pool to save memory), and hash code stability (cached hashCode for HashMap keys).

interviewQuestions.question: How does HashMap handle collisions in Java 8+?
interviewQuestions.answer: HashMap uses an array of buckets. When two keys hash to the same bucket index, they form a linked list. Once a single bucket reaches a threshold (TREEIFY_THRESHOLD = 8) and total table capacity is at least 64, the linked list transforms into a balanced red-black tree, reducing lookup time from O(n) to O(log n).

interviewQuestions.question: What are Virtual Threads in Java 21, and how do they differ from Platform Threads?
interviewQuestions.answer: Platform threads are 1:1 wrappers around OS threads with ~1MB memory overhead and expensive context switching. Virtual threads are user-mode threads managed by the JVM with tiny memory footprints (~few hundred bytes). When a virtual thread performs blocking I/O, the JVM unmounts it from the carrier OS thread, enabling millions of concurrent connections on standard hardware.
